name: Prescribing of Amino Acid Formula (AAF) and Extensively Hydrolysed Formula (eHF))
title: Amino acid formula (AAF) as proportion of AAF and extensively hydrolysed formula (eHF)
description: Prescribing of amino acid formula (AAF) products as proportion of AAF and extensively hydrolysed formula (eHF)
y_label: Percentage of CMPA products (eHF + AAF) prescribed as AAF
why_it_matters: These products are prescribed for a number of allergy indications, and are most commonly prescribed for Cow's Milk Protein Allergy
NICE Clinical Knowledge Summary for Cows' Milk Allergy in children outlines the use of hypoallergenic infant formulas. It
states that extensively hydrolysed formulas (EHFs) are usually used first-line. They are whey- or casein-based and are generally well
tolerated by infants and children with cow's milk allergy. Amino acid formulas (AAFs) should be reserved for children with severe
symptoms of IgE- or non-IgE-mediated allergy or a history of anaphylaxis; those who cannot tolerate EHFs or have ongoing symptoms
with them; and those whose symptoms do not respond to maternal avoidance of cow's milk or who have symptoms while exclusively breastfeeding.
Amino acid formula (AAF) products are almost three times more expensive than EHF, and it is believed that only a small proportion of infants
need to be started on AAF for CMPA in primary care.
